title: Agent Security Assurance Attestation (ASAS-A) v0.1
description: Draft specification. A machine-readable attestation that a third party can verify offline, with no network access and no trust in the issuer. Closed schemas are deliberate: `additionalProperties: false` is what makes 'no argument values' and 'unknown must be declared' enforceable by a validator instead of by promise.

asas.description: Spec version this attestation conforms to.

environment.description: prod / staging / a named fleet; free text but must be present when the org has more than one.

scope.description: What was in scope (e.g. 'all Codex agents on macOS laptops'). Readers must not infer coverage beyond this list.

agents.description: ASAS-1.1. Every agent that was in scope MUST appear here.

owner.description: ASAS-1.1. A named human responsible for this agent. 'platform team' is not a person.

registered.description: ASAS-1.2/1.3. false = shadow agent; it MUST also be listed as restricted in boundaries.

shared.description: ASAS-1.4. true = more than one agent uses this credential, which MUST be reported as a violation.

delegation.description: ASAS-2.4/2.5. Present only when this agent received permissions from another agent.

from.description: agent id that granted the delegation

assets.description: ASAS-3. External components the agents can reach.

version.description: null = version not determined, which MUST appear in unknown[] (same rule as contentHash / pinned).

declaredRef.description: What the configuration actually says (e.g. 'chrome-devtools-mcp@latest'). Kept separate from `version` so a diff never mistakes 'resolved the reference' for 'the version changed' - that false positive was found by running the diff on real attestations.

pinned.description: ASAS-3.1. false requires exemptUntil. null means 'not determined' and MUST appear in unknown[] - a producer that cannot tell whether something is pinned must say so rather than guess.

exemptUntil.description: ASAS-3.1. A written exemption with an expiry date. Open-ended exemptions are not conformant.

contentHash.description: ASAS-3.2. null is allowed and means 'not determined' - it then MUST appear in unknown[]. Forging a hash is worse than admitting you could not compute one. (Amended 2026-09-20 while writing the reference builder: the original draft required a hash for every asset, which would have forced producers to invent one.)

descHash.description: ASAS-3.3. Hash of the tool description + schema. Tracked separately from contentHash so description-level tampering is visible even when the artifact is unchanged.

reachableTools.description: null = tool surface not enumerated (e.g. --introspect not run, or the server failed to answer). MUST appear in unknown[].

verdicts.description: ASAS-2.2. Every decision carries the reason it was made. A verdict without a basis is not conformant, and a validator can enforce that.

basis.description: The literal reason: matched rule, matched keyword, or 'observed N times'. Empty or 'n/a' is not conformant.

unknown.description: ASAS-3.5. Enumerated failures MUST be declared here. An empty array is allowed; omitting the field is not. Hiding unknowns is attestation fraud.

observations.description: ASAS-5.1/5.2. Tool-level counts only. The closed schema is what enforces 'never record argument values': there is no field to put them in.

argKeys.description: Names of the arguments used. Values MUST NOT appear anywhere in this document.

mode.description: ASAS-4.1. 'readonly' is a legitimate answer and MUST be declared rather than implied.

revocationMinutes.description: ASAS-8.1. How long it takes to revoke all permissions of one agent.

signals.description: S1-S6 counts. Metadata only: no payloads, no prompts, no tool arguments.

compliance.description: ASAS-7.2. Maps evidence to framework clauses. Claiming compliance is explicitly out of scope.

statement.const: Supports evidence for the listed requirements. Does not assert compliance.

signature.description: ASAS-6.4. Optional. Signature MUST NOT be a prerequisite for verification.
